executiveSummary: Wildfires across France and Spain escalated into one of the region’s most disruptive fire emergencies in recent years, forcing between 220,000 and 300,000 people to evacuate, closing Bordeaux Airport, and straining emergency services; reporting varies by outlet and timing. View Article Supporting Report Typhoon Noul triggered major relocations in southern China and Hong Kong, with authorities moving approximately 715,000–801,000 people and reporting at least 21 injuries, alongside large-scale transport disruption. View Article Security Advisory In Afghanistan’s Nuristan province, flash floods destroyed homes and shops, with at least 23 people dead and more than 100 missing; communities remain isolated and at risk of additional flooding. View Article Texas faced successive rounds of severe flooding with mandatory evacuations, hundreds of rescues, and multiple fatalities reported across the Hill Country and South Texas. View Article Supporting Report France’s June heat wave produced severe public health impacts, with at least 5,700 excess deaths reported by Public Health France. View Article Additional humanitarian needs persist after recent earthquakes in Venezuela, and monsoon flooding in Bangladesh and regional flooding in Chile continue to affect large populations and require sustained assistance. France/Spain: Fire conditions may remain elevated where heat and wind persist; expect dynamic evacuation perimeters and periodic road/rail/airport disruptions near active fronts. Afghanistan (Nuristan): Search and rescue and relief access remain weather-contingent; additional rainfall would elevate secondary hazards. Texas (US): Localized flood hazards may linger along river corridors; community re-entry and damage assessments ongoing where water recedes. Bangladesh/Chile: Monsoon/seasonal flood impacts likely to sustain humanitarian needs; watch for disease risk in crowded shelters and low-lying areas. Central US heat: Continued health risk for exposed/vulnerable groups; cooling access and outreach remain priorities.
